_what: Every file and folder the Trillion programs on this computer keep under the person's home (computer/device-stores.mjs): where it is, what it holds (secret, content, settings or cache), the access it must have, how long it may be kept, and whether it is sealed. `audit` says what differs from this list and what lies under a root that no row names; `repair` puts modes right, makes missing folders and links, deletes what has outlived its retention, and writes a receipt. A new store is a new row. Nothing here names a store in code. At every start the Mac host asks for an `audit` in a worker of its own (mac-tools.json on_start) and keeps its counts in `audit_file`; `repair_at_start` lists the row ids it also repairs then (none by default).

rows.what: The folder holding the trillion command's own copy; its files keep their program modes.
The trillion command on the person's PATH (harness/trillion.json install.link); remade when it points elsewhere or is gone.
The key this computer's trillion command made, when it is kept in a file.
Which tool programs the account installed for this Mac.
Completed tool answers waiting for the account to accept them (and their numbered copies).
What the computer reader read, with its drives and lock.
Messages and sessions of services carried on this computer.
Audio and notes of listening.
The speech-to-text socket and its working files.
The speaker socket and its notices.
Who people are, learned from contacts.
The Mac's copy of the person's records.
The Trillion drive's journals and cache.
Events and settings of the chats Trillion wakes.
Files written by AIs and what was sent.
Web chats kept.
Messages recorded as they are sent.
Holds that keep this Mac awake.
Decisions owed, and their draining and pace files.
Decisions already drained.
Chats kept from the person's AI apps.
The work-taking helper's state.
The work-taking hook's state.
Setup progress.
The person's screen permissions and taint.
The loopback executor's per-install secret.
Helpers fetched on first use (computer/helper-runtimes.mjs); their files keep their own execute bit.
What the last repair changed.
The counts of the last start-up audit of this list (names and modes only).
The Mac host's own log, sealed for a reader; written only when a reader key is set (mac-tools.json host_log).

words.wrong_mode: {path} is open to more than its owner ({have}, should be {want}).
words.expired: {path} is older than the {days} days it may be kept.
words.unlisted: {path} is kept here but no row says what it holds, who may read it or how long it stays.
words.plaintext_content: {id} holds the person's content in files anyone with this account on this Mac can read; no row seals it.
